states.description: Core body temperature in degrees Celsius

scenario_text: Track core body temperature during recovery from a mild thermal displacement under constant environmental conditions. The body stores heat while fixed metabolic production and temperature-dependent heat loss determine the net rate of temperature change. In the baseline model, aggregate thermoregulatory heat loss changes smoothly around a fixed thermal set point, producing monotonic relaxation. Humidity, clothing, activity, and ambient temperature remain fixed throughout each trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Whole-body heat storage
Constant baseline metabolic heat production
Aggregate heat loss that increases with core temperature relative to fixed surroundings
Instantaneous homeostatic adjustment represented by a smooth restoring response
baseline_assumptions: The body is a single well-mixed thermal compartment
Ambient conditions, clothing, and activity are constant
Effective heat capacity is constant
Sweating, vasomotor responses, and metabolic thermogenesis are combined into one instantaneous heat-loss response
scientific_constraints: Core temperature must remain finite and physiologically plausible
The net thermal response must point toward the stable equilibrium near baseline
Heat loss cannot be negative under the fixed ordinary environment
The equilibrium must be locally stable
refinement_agenda: Add a sweating threshold and saturation limit
Separate core and skin temperatures
Introduce delayed vasomotor control
Allow shivering thermogenesis below a recruitment threshold
Release the fixed-environment assumption to include changing ambient temperature or humidity

domain_mechanisms.description: negative feedback around a physiological set point
finite storage, transport, or organ capacity
